subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Bodhidharma's Eyelids
description: Learn Bodhidharma's Eyelids in one minute.

hook.text: A Buddhist legend says tea grew from the severed eyelids of Bodhidharma, the monk who brought Zen to China.

buildup.text: Bodhidharma vowed to meditate for nine years without sleeping. When his eyelids drooped, he cut them off in frustration.

discovery.text: Where his eyelids fell, tea bushes sprouted. The leaves carried his determination—keeping all who drink them awake.

twist.text: This legend is more popular in Japan than China. It connects tea directly to Zen discipline and spiritual endurance.

climax.text: The eyelid myth explains why tea and Zen monasteries are inseparable in East Asian culture. Tea sustains meditation.

punchline.text: Severed eyelids, sprouting bushes, endless wakefulness. Tea's darkest origin story.

quiz.question: According to the legend, why does tea keep people awake?
options: It came from a magical spring
It grew from Bodhidharma's severed eyelids, carrying his determination

details.summary: In Buddhist legend, the monk Bodhidharma cut off his eyelids to stay awake during meditation. Where the eyelids fell, tea plants grew. This dramatic origin story links tea to spiritual discipline and explains why tea became the beverage of Buddhist monks across Asia.
details.whyItMatters: The Bodhidharma legend connects tea to Zen Buddhism and monastic practice, establishing the spiritual dimension that distinguishes tea culture from coffee culture.
takeaways: Bodhidharma supposedly grew tea plants from his severed eyelids
The legend connects tea directly to Buddhist meditation practice
It explains tea's deep association with spiritual discipline in Asia

faq.question: Who was Bodhidharma and why is he important in tea history?
faq.answer: Bodhidharma was a legendary Indian monk who brought Chan Buddhism to China, which later became Zen in Japan. His mythical connection to tea helped establish it as the sacred beverage of Buddhist monasteries across East Asia.

faq.question: Is the Bodhidharma tea legend more Chinese or Japanese in origin?
faq.answer: The legend has versions in both Chinese and Japanese traditions, reflecting Bodhidharma's journey from India through China. Japanese Zen culture particularly embraced the story to explain tea's role in meditation.
